situational.label: Situational
situational.meaning: Pulled when the Situation Map sends you there.

tiers.rule: Tier badge on every protocol card, app page and Manual chapter opener; text label always shown beside the dots.

protocols.name: Green Rule (Safety Gate)
canonical: Comes before every other tool in the system.
Afraid of your partner, being threatened, or not free to say no? → Stop. These tools are not for this. Get outside help (see Help Lines).
Pause + Return is for flooding, never for fear: if threats, fear, coercion or violence appear, do not return at the set time; leave safely and use Help Lines.

protocols.name: Pause + Return
canonical: Exact return time, always.
For flooding, never for fear.

protocols.name: 60-Second Alliance Reset
canonical: Five steps: Stop · Say it · Touch (only if welcome) · Breathe (three slow breaths) · Return (exact time).
Always pair stopping with a real return time.
canonicalPhrases: I want to connect, not fight.

protocols.name: Micro-Repair
canonical: Timing window (use everywhere, no 10-minute or 48-hour variants).
canonicalPhrases: start within minutes if you can; complete within 24 hours

protocols.name: Weekly Reset
canonical: 5 parts, about 40 minutes: Appreciation (5 min) · Check the load (15 min) · One friction point (15 min) · Requests + Next steps (5 min).
Set a 40-minute timer.
The monthly Care Check-in (inside the Weekly Reset) happens in 'Check the load' once a month; never a separate meeting.
Maintenance, not a trial. Flooded? Pause + Return first.
canonicalPhrases: the monthly Care Check-in (inside the Weekly Reset)

protocols.name: System Overlay
protocols.plainEnglishSubtitle: spotting the pattern you're both stuck in
canonical: Five steps: Warm up · Make it safe · Say what happened · Ask for one thing · Agree on next steps.

protocols.name: Conflict Protocol
canonical: Check if you're calm first; overwhelmed → Pause + Return.
Listen in order: impact first, what would help second, their side last.

protocols.name: Proof Protocol
protocols.plainEnglishSubtitle: a specific change, evidence you can both see, and a set time window
canonical: Proof = a specific change, evidence you can both see, and a set time window.
Record it simply, to see and review at the agreed check-in (never 'track'/'verify' the partner).

protocols.name: Trust Recovery
canonical: Only the partner who broke trust acknowledges impact; the hurt partner is never asked to confess in return.
Transparency is offered voluntarily by the partner who broke trust, time-limited, and never becomes monitoring (no demanding passwords, location tracking, or reading messages).

Sexual pressure: a no met with pressure once → Green Rule / Trust Recovery conversation; again, or either feels unable to say no → stop and use the Help Lines. If it involved force, threats or fear, it isn't a 'once': go straight to the Help Lines.
Deciding not to rebuild, or to end the relationship, is a valid outcome of this protocol, not a failure of it.

protocols.name: Full Recovery
canonical: Six steps; calm, agreed, scheduled — never mid-fight or sprung on someone.
One-sided breach: only the partner who caused it acknowledges impact. Closing line only if it's true for both of you.
Routed from Uninvestment Check at 3 or more signs: book within a week.
Deciding not to rebuild, or to end the relationship, is a valid outcome of this protocol, not a failure of it.

protocols.name: Uninvestment Check

bands.0–2: likely needs space and small repairs (Micro-Repair, Morning + Evening Rhythm)
bands.3 or more: may be pulling away → book a Full Recovery within a week

canonical: Describe observable behaviour; don't claim to know the partner's intent ('may be pulling away', not 'is preparing to leave').
If contempt is one of your signs, skip the count: contempt means stop and get outside support first.
Contempt, fear or coercion at any count → safety and outside support first.
Trust breach → Trust Recovery; 3+ signs → Full Recovery within a week.
Deciding not to rebuild, or to end the relationship, is a valid outcome of this protocol, not a failure of it.
signs: doing more on your own in place of shared time (time apart is healthy)

protocols.name: Unity Anchor
canonical: Situation Map row: Outside pressure or disapproval from family, friends or strangers → Unity Anchor.
Unity Anchor decides how the COUPLE responds to outside pressure, never how much access a relative gets to your partner.
No tool is ever used to limit a partner's contact with friends, family, money, phone or movement.
canonicalPhrases: We're on the same side of this.

protocols.name: Morning + Evening Rhythm
canonical: Morning check-in 5 min or less; evening check-in about 10 min.
Physical contact is always 'if welcome'.

protocols.name: Intimacy Pact
canonical: A “no” needs no script, reason, or substitute offer. No pact or agreement creates an obligation to sex, touch, or disclosure.
Physical contact is always 'if welcome'.

A no met with pressure once → Green Rule / Trust Recovery conversation; again, or either feels unable to say no → stop and use the Help Lines. If it involved force, threats or fear, it isn't a 'once': go straight to the Help Lines.

protocols.name: Consistency Pact
canonical: Private weekly check; does not replace being accountable to your partner for a real breach.

sun-memory.name: Sun Memory

lengths.quick: a few minutes, inside one ritual (stop the checklist, return to ease)
lengths.full: agree a stretch of 2 to 24 hours with no talk about tools or fixes

canonical: Pauses system-talk only, never basic communication, safety, childcare/logistics, or a scheduled repair.
Either partner may end it by naming a safety concern.
All Sun Memory safety rules apply to both lengths.
'Kill-Switch' never appears in buyer-facing text (retired in Round 10).

guardrails.safety-first-row: Afraid of your partner, being threatened, or not free to say no? → Stop. These tools are not for this. Get outside help (see Help Lines).
guardrails.leaving-is-valid: Deciding not to rebuild, or to end the relationship, is a valid outcome of this protocol, not a failure of it.
guardrails.one-sided-breach: When one partner caused the breach, only that partner acknowledges impact; the hurt partner is never asked to confess in return. Closing/reconciliation lines are optional ('only if it's true for both of you').
guardrails.no-script-no: A “no” needs no script, reason, or substitute offer. No pact or agreement creates an obligation to sex, touch, or disclosure.
guardrails.no-limiting-contact: No tool is ever used to limit a partner's contact with friends, family, money, phone or movement.
guardrails.no-monitoring: Never 'track'/'verify' the other partner; use 'see and review at the agreed check-in'. Transparency is voluntary, time-limited, never monitoring.
guardrails.sexual-pressure: A no met with pressure once → Green Rule / Trust Recovery conversation; if it happens again, or either of you feels unable to say no → stop and use the Help Lines. If it involved force, threats or fear, it isn't a 'once': go straight to the Help Lines.
guardrails.misuse-label: 'Abuse' is reserved for abuse; a guardrail about avoidance/misuse of a tool is a 'Misuse guardrail'.
